parsed.notes: Lens B only; support and quote-fidelity issues were not reviewed except where support payloads embedded treatment or currency claims.

reasons: The lake identity matches Frank v. Maryland, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1959-05-04, docket 278, cluster_id 105880.
The lake citations include official cite 359 U.S. 360, parallel cites 79 S. Ct. 804 and 3 L. Ed. 2d 877, and vendor-neutral cite 1959 U.S. LEXIS 1085.
No current-good-law status is asserted in this case-cite payload; treatment is reviewed separately.
residual_risks: The lake treatment fields are unverified, so this existence check does not establish live-law status.

defect.evidence_quote: Frontier stub: treatment/progeny intentionally not derived until S6 promotion.
defect.locator_note: holding field; treatment clause after the dash
defect.problem: The holding payload embeds a treatment assertion that the rule was overruled by Camara, but the disclosed lake record has treatment unverified and no treatment or progeny edge to Camara.
defect.proposed_fix: Remove or caveat the overruled-by-Camara clause until the lake record includes certified treatment/progeny evidence, or supply the Camara authority record and edge.

reasons: Lens B does not assess the underlying holding support or quote fidelity.
The only disclosed treatment judgment is unverified; lake treatment.edges is empty and progeny rows_cached is 0.
Under the default-to-refuted rule, the overruled-by-Camara treatment claim cannot stand from the disclosed evidence.
residual_risks: Camara may support this outside the disclosed record, but that evidence is not present here.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep the holding limited to Frank itself, and put any Camara overrule statement behind certified treatment evidence.

defect.evidence_quote: Frontier stub: treatment/progeny intentionally not derived until S6 promotion.
defect.locator_note: home role for Special Needs and Administrative Searches
defect.problem: The home role labels the case as Historical / origin; the Historical status is a treatment/currency label, but the disclosed lake treatment record is unverified and has no derived treatment or progeny.
defect.proposed_fix: Change the role to an origin-only label with treatment unverified, or certify the historical/overruled status in the lake record before using Historical.

reasons: Lens B does not decide whether Frank is substantively an origin case.
The disclosed treatment fields do not verify that Frank is historical rather than live law.
Default-to-refuted applies because the currency component of the role is not verifiable from the disclosed record.
residual_risks: The origin component may be supportable under lens A, but the Historical currency label needs treatment evidence.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use 'Origin - treatment unverified' until treatment promotion supplies the overrule history.

reasons: The content treatment payload matches the lake treatment fields: field_i_validity unverified, composite_basis unverified, as_of_content null, and as_of_treatment null.
The scope note matches the lake record and accurately discloses that treatment/progeny have not been derived.
No disclosed lake edge supersedes or contradicts the unverified treatment status.
residual_risks: This standing unverified treatment field does not validate the page's separate overruled-by-Camara narrative.

defect.problem: The weight label 'Binding - SCOTUS' is not verifiable as a current-law weight from the disclosed treatment record. The lake verifies SCOTUS identity, but treatment/good-law status is unverified and no no-negative-treatment judgment is supplied.
defect.proposed_fix: Separate court hierarchy from current precedential force, e.g. 'SCOTUS - treatment unverified,' or certify treatment before using a Binding label.

reasons: The lake identity supports only the SCOTUS court label.
The lake treatment fields do not verify that Frank remains binding live law for the asserted proposition.
Under lens B, a Binding weight label cannot stand without disclosed good-law/treatment support.
residual_risks: If authority_weight is intended only as issuing-court hierarchy, the label should be renamed so it does not imply current binding force.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use a non-live-law hierarchy label unless and until treatment is certified.
